title: Furniture, Objects, and Shopping
summary: Common objects, products, prices, and shopping situations.
whyItMatters: Everyday objects give you immediate language for your home, classroom, office, and shops. Learning them with articles, plurals, colors, and practical categories makes the vocabulary usable rather than a disconnected list.

mentalModel.title: Organize objects by place
mentalModel.content: Group vocabulary into scenes you can picture: furniture in a room, technology on a desk, and products in a shop.

mentalModel.title: Learn a three-part noun package
mentalModel.content: Record each noun with its article and plural: der Tisch – die Tische, die Lampe – die Lampen, das Sofa – die Sofas.

mentalModel.title: Attach one visible property
mentalModel.content: Make each object memorable with a color, size, or condition: der rote Stuhl, die kleine Lampe, das neue Handy.

ruleBlocks.title: Learn article, noun, and plural together
ruleBlocks.content: A useful vocabulary entry contains three parts: 'der Stuhl – die Stühle'. This prepares you to recognize gender and talk about more than one object.

ruleBlocks.title: Build vocabulary around places
ruleBlocks.content: Use a room, desk, or shop as a visual map. Place each new noun in a scene instead of memorizing it in isolation.

ruleBlocks.title: Describe what buyers can see
ruleBlocks.content: At A1, the most useful properties are color, size, age or condition, and price: blau, groß, neu, gebraucht, billig, teuer.

patterns: article + noun: der Tisch, die Lampe, das Sofa
singular → plural: der Stuhl → die Stühle
in a shop: product + price + basic property
sentenceStructure: Use a short 'sein' sentence to describe an object: 'Die Lampe ist modern.'
Use 'haben' to state what is available: 'Wir haben einen Tisch.'
Use 'suchen' or 'brauchen' to name a shopping goal.
Keep the article attached when naming an unfamiliar object.

concepts: recognize noun gender and basic plurals
describe rooms, ownership, and household needs
manage returns, recommendations, and detailed comparisons

comparisons.summary: This theme supplies the nouns. The grammar lesson explains why each noun uses der, die, or das and how indefinite articles work.
The communication lesson uses these objects and properties in practical shopping questions and answers.

examples.de: Im Zimmer sind ein Tisch, zwei Stühle und eine Lampe.
examples.en: There are a table, two chairs, and a lamp in the room.

examples.de: Das Handy ist neu und sehr teuer.
examples.en: The phone is new and very expensive.

examples.de: Ich suche eine kleine schwarze Tasche.
examples.en: I am looking for a small black bag.

examples.de: Der Computer ist gebraucht, aber schnell.
examples.en: The computer is used but fast.

examples.de: Die Stühle sind modern und bequem.
examples.en: The chairs are modern and comfortable.

commonMistakes.correct: Learn: der Tisch – die Tische = table.
commonMistakes.reason: The article and plural are part of the practical noun package.
The definite article for all plural nouns is 'die' in the basic nominative form.

commonMistakes.wrong: Guess an article from the object's meaning.
commonMistakes.correct: Learn the article with each noun.
commonMistakes.reason: Grammatical gender is a property of the German noun and often cannot be predicted from meaning.

specialCases: Plural formation varies: some nouns add -e or -en, some change a vowel, and some remain similar. Learn the plural with the noun.
Loanwords such as 'das Sofa' and 'das Handy' have German articles and German plural patterns.
Colors are written in lowercase when used as ordinary adjectives: blau, rot, schwarz.
tips: Label five real objects around you with article, noun, and plural.
Create a tiny product card containing a noun, color, condition, and imagined price.
Review vocabulary by room or shopping category rather than alphabetically.

memoryHooks.title: Every noun travels as a trio
memoryHooks.content: Article, singular, plural: der Tisch, der Tisch, die Tische.

memoryHooks.title: Build a mental showroom
memoryHooks.content: Place furniture and products in an imaginary shop, then attach one visible property to each item.
